title: Lena and the Songbook
premise: For ten years, Mara Winterbourne has written anonymous letters to the residents of Gullwrack Cove, tucked into the pages of a battered songbook that circulates through the village like a tide. When Elias Thorne—the man she once loved and lost, now a widowed musician—moves into the cottage next door, he begins hunting the letter-writer whose words kept him alive through his darkest year. As Mara helps him restore the lighthouse and their old love rekindles, she must decide whether revealing herself will heal him or shatter the fragile family they've built. In the end, with her grandmother's memory fading and the songbook's final page blank, Mara signs her name at last—and learns that truth, spoken in time, is its own kind of homecoming.
about_author: P. M. Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's letters before writing fiction of her own. She lives on a windswept coast where she collects sea glass, old songs, and stories about the things we almost say.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara tends the decommissioned lighthouse and writes her tenth anonymous letter into the circulating songbook, hiding grief for her late grandmother behind routine. A moving van arrives at the neighboring cottage. Emotional beat: comfortable solitude cracked by an unexpected arrival.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Familiar Hands
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara recognizes Elias Thorne unloading boxes—older, wearier, carrying a guitar case she once knew intimately. He doesn't recognize her behind her garden fence. Emotional beat: panic disguised as politeness; the past knocking loudly.

chapters.title: What the Songbook Carries
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias unpacks and finds his own decade-old copy of the songbook, filled with anonymous letters that pulled him through his wife's illness and death. He resolves to find the writer. Emotional beat: gratitude sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Tea and Small Lies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Elias knocks with housewarming bread; Mara serves tea while concealing that she knows him from a summer ten years ago. Her neighbor Dot interrupts, treating them like a matched set already. Emotional beat: warmth blooming inside deception.

chapters.title: Ten Summers Ago
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, interwoven flashback. The summer they met: music on the lighthouse gallery, a kiss interrupted by her father's death, and her flight to London without goodbye. Emotional beat: understanding why silence became her native language.

chapters.title: The Village Keeps Its Secrets
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias asks around about the letter-writer; villagers protectively deflect, and Dot warns him some gifts are better anonymous. Meanwhile Mara fixes his crooked gate without being asked. Emotional beat: the town as a found family guarding one of its own.

chapters.title: Chords in the Dark
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A storm knocks out power; Elias plays by candlelight on the shared beach path, and Mara joins him singing a song only the two of them know. He freezes—he's heard that harmony somewhere before. Emotional beat: memory surfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: Dot's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Dot reveals she has known Mara was the letter-writer for years and kept the secret; she urges confession before Elias finds out another way. Mara refuses, terrified of becoming responsible for his grief twice over. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made explicit.

chapters.title: The Letter That Saved Him
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias reads Mara's most desperate letter aloud at the pub's open mic, telling the room this stranger's words stopped him from walking into the sea. Mara listens from the back, undone. Emotional beat: her invisibility transformed into unbearable intimacy.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On the lighthouse gallery where they once kissed, Elias leans in—and Mara pulls away, confessing nothing but leaving him confused and stung. Emotional beat: the rehearsed sentence rising in her throat and dying there.

chapters.title: Diagnosis
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias receives news his mother's dementia is advancing rapidly and she is moving to Gullwrack's care home; time, he tells Mara, feels suddenly short. He asks her to help him finish restoring the lighthouse lamp for his mother to see. Emotional beat: urgency entering the story's bloodstream.

chapters.title: Three Hands and a Lamp
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Mara, Elias, and his mother Agnes polish the Fresnel lens together; Agnes mistakes Mara for 'the girl from the photographs' Elias keeps hidden. Mara sees her own younger face in his wallet. Emotional beat: tenderness braided with dread of exposure.

chapters.title: The Photographs
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alone, Elias studies the photos and finally places Mara: the girl from ten summers ago who vanished. He says nothing, testing whether she'll tell him herself. Emotional beat: quiet betrayal beginning to calcify.

chapters.title: Agnes Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In a lucid moment, Agnes tells Mara she knows about the letters—she found the songbook drafts in Elias's flat—and begs her not to let her son lose the same woman twice. Emotional beat: the secret now held by three people and cracking.

chapters.title: The Wrong Confession
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confronts Mara about the past, and she admits she left without goodbye—but still cannot claim the letters. Feeling her honesty incomplete, he withdraws coldly. Emotional beat: half-truths wounding more than silence.

chapters.title: Blank Page
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The songbook returns to Mara for its final entry before being retired to the village archive, its last page blank. Dot falls ill, and the community rallies—reminding Mara what found family means and what cowardice costs. Emotional beat: the cost of waiting made visible.

chapters.title: What Dot Knew
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hospital-bound Dot, fearing she won't get to see it resolved, leaves Elias a note naming Mara as the letter-writer. He reads it alone in the corridor, ten years of gratitude and deception colliding. Emotional beat: revelation as both gift and wound.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Goes Dark
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias cancels the lamp-lighting ceremony and prepares to leave Gullwrack, feeling his whole recovery was built on someone else's fiction. Mara watches his packed car from the gallery window. Emotional beat: rock bottom; the family fracturing.

chapters.title: The Sentence Rehearsed for a Decade
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the ceremony's empty hour, Mara climbs the tower, lights the lamp herself, and speaks the rehearsed sentence aloud to the dark—to no one, then, hearing footsteps, to him. Emotional beat: climax; truth finally outrunning fear.

chapters.title: Every Word Was You
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Elias, drawn back by the lit lamp, hears Mara's full confession—every letter, every reason, every year. Anger gives way to grief gives way to recognition: the voice that saved him was hers all along. Emotional beat: catharsis; forgiveness chosen, not owed.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara writes the songbook's final letter signed with her name, and the village gathers as it's read aloud—Dot recovering, Agnes present, Elias holding her hand. Emotional beat: private devotion becoming public belonging.

chapters.title: Homecoming Tide
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. One year later: the restored lighthouse glows, Elias plays on the gallery, and Mara begins a new novel whose first line is the sentence she once couldn't say. Emotional beat: resolution—love in the present tense, at last.
